title: South Korea issues guidelines on using generative AI for mental-health support
source_used: Seoul Economic Daily (MLex pool link is paywalled, no article text)
key_facts: The Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Korean Neuropsychiatric Association released the 'Guidelines for Using Generative AI for Mental Health Purposes' on 8 October 2026, ahead of World Mental Health Day on 10 October.
The guidelines cover protecting personal information, guarding against inaccurate information and preventing overdependence on AI, with separate guidance for children, adolescents and guardians.
A Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs survey of 1,019 people aged 15 to 79 who had used generative AI in the past month (25 Aug to 4 Sep) found 68.8% used it for emotional purposes.
Of all respondents, 14.6% said they had judged themselves to have a specific mental illness based on AI conversations, or had accepted AI's answer as a diagnosis.
16.3% said they kept talking to AI when they were trying to focus on real-world tasks; 51.7% of adolescents aged 15 to 18 said they were more dependent on AI than other people.
86.9% said government guidance or regulation on AI use is needed.
quote_evidence: The Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Korean Neuropsychiatric Association released the "Guidelines for Using Generative AI for Mental Health Purposes" on the 8th, ahead of World Mental Health Day on Oct. 10.
68.8% said they used AI for emotional purposes such as everyday conversation, emotional connection or psychological counseling.
why_it_matters_hint: Official guidance on AI for emotional support matters to people who talk to chatbots about feelings and to parents of teenagers.
notes: MLex original is paywalled (no article text); Seoul Economic Daily English edition read instead. Survey figures are self-reported by respondents. Korean outlets Chosunbiz, Korea Biomedical Review and Asia Economy carry the same release.
